title: Rav Chilkiyah bar Tuvi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Rav’s student, as in [Bava Batra 39b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.39b.4): Giddel bar Minyomi (he is Rav Giddel without further designation) had a protest to make. He found Rav Huna, Chiyya bar Rav and Rav Chilkiyah bar Tuvi sitting and protested before them. The next year he came again to protest. They told him that he need not protest again and cited Rav, etc. In [Gittin 57a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.57a.14): Rav Minyomi bar Chilkiyah, Rav Chilkiyah bar Tuvia and Rav Huna bar Chiyya were sitting together; they said, “If anyone has heard something about Kefar Sikhnya of Egypt, let him say it,” etc.

His halakhot we find in [Shabbat 97a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.97a.14), [Eruvin 28b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.28b.22) and [Yoma 63a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.63a.14), and Hyman proposes reading “Rav Chilkiyah bar Tuvi” in [Zevachim 114b:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.114b.11).[^3] He worked his land and found his bread from it, as in [Menachot 85b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.85b.6): he had a corner of land; he plowed half and sowed half, and it yielded twofold, and he sold the wheat for fine flour.[^2]

notes.text: ועבדה על חד תרי means that the land yielded twofold, not that he worked it twice. Supplied Menachot25b is retained alongside the matching saved Davidson85b. The source’s abbreviated account is not expanded with an extra repeated plowing clause.

The consulted Gittin and Eruvin give the name Tuvia. The farming account is at Menachot 85b. That passage describes alternating the ground he plowed and sowed and says the land yielded double. Hyman abridges the repeated plowing and sowing. The supplied Hebrew has כה: for the farming account.
The linked text gives Rabbi Chilkiyah with the parenthetical word דבי before Rav Tuvi. Davidson understands it as “from the school of Rav Tuvi.” The patronymic here is Hyman’s proposed reading.
